subject: Dedicated pool service-level amendment & queueing playbook
messages:
From: Nina Park <nina.park@starlit.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-18T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated pool — request for SLA amendment around queueing/tail latency

Hi Sean,

Hope you’re well. I’m leading infrastructure at Starlit AI (we use Redwood Dedicated for our production LLM endpoints). Over the last two quarters we’ve seen recurring tail-latency events during our nightly retraining and batch traffic windows that are impacting SLAs for downstream customers.

Our ask: can Redwood provide an amendment to our Dedicated pool SLA that includes two items:

- Guaranteed reserved headroom (burst reservation) for our pool during scheduled windows (we’re proposing a 10% headroom carved out of our committed GPUs).
- Queueing priority for a specific model variant (starlit-prod-v2) so critical inference traffic is admitted ahead of low-priority batch jobs during contention.

We’re trying to avoid running more redundant infrastructure and would prefer a contract amendment rather than immediate capacity increases. Please let me know what information you need (current committed GPU count: 60 gpus; typical sustained steady-state RPS: ~1,100 requests/min; peak windows: daily 02:00–05:00 UTC with short spikes up to 5x).

If useful I can pull our tail-latency SLO violations and a short diagram of our traffic profile. We’d like an initial feasibility and cost estimate in the next 7–10 business days.

Thanks —
Nina Park
Head of Infrastructure, Starlit AI
procurement@starlit.ai

(attachment: starlit-dedicated-asks.pdf)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Nina Park <nina.park@starlit.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-19T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool — request for SLA amendment around queueing/tail latency

Hi Nina — thanks for the clear note and the numbers, this is helpful.

Looping in Marissa (account lead) and Karthik (SRE/Product) to scope feasibility and a commercial approach. A few clarifying Qs we’ll need to size an amendment:

- When you say 10% headroom, do you mean 10% of committed GPUs reserved (e.g., 6 GPUs out of 60) or 10% of expected CPU/GPU utilisation headroom?
- Can you share an anonymized sample of a 24-hour RPS timeline (UTC) and the hourly token distribution? That helps with batching and KV-cache sizing.
- Are the peak spikes at predictable cadence (e.g., aligned to ETL/retrain jobs) or bursty and random?

Marissa/Karthik — can you review internal constraints we need to account for: queue preemption behavior, priority token admission, and whether we can map a model-variant-level priority without impacting overall pool fairness? If there are obvious cost levers (burst reservation pricing, guaranteed concurrency slabs), flag them and we’ll include in the response.

I’ll coordinate a 30–60 minute call next week after we have a first-pass feasibility note.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-22T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool — request for SLA amendment around queueing/tail latency

On Dec 19, 2026, Sean Gallagher wrote:
> Marissa/Karthik — can you review internal constraints we need to account for: queue preemption behavior, priority token admission, and whether we can map a model-variant-level priority without impacting overall pool fairness?

Quick internal runbook / proposed amendment summary below (first pass):

- Reserved headroom: add a "burst reservation" equal to 6 GPUs (10% of committed 60 GPU capacity). Reservation is billed as an additive monthly fee and guarantees capacity during contention windows.
- Priority admission: create a model-variant priority token for "starlit-prod-v2". Priority will operate as soft-preemption: high-priority requests are admitted ahead of best-effort batches but will not evict in-progress high-priority inference. This avoids cold model reload churn.
- Queueing SLOs (proposed): 95th percentile latency target for standard gen (<= 120ms for requests <= 512 tokens), 99th percentile <= 400ms. Tail exceptions tied to documented scheduled maintenance windows.
- Maintenance carveouts: allow up to two scheduled maintenance windows/month where we can perform rolling maintenance with reduced headroom guarantees (must be pre-notified 72 hours).
- Telemetry & regression alarms: include a shared dashboard link and a weekly digest of SLO violations for 90 days post-amendment.
- Pricing: propose a fixed monthly burden for burst reservation + incremental per-token surcharge for prioritized admission above a threshold. Exact numbers to be provided after Karthik's capacity model.

Attachments I will send with the external reply: SLA-amendment-diff.pdf (redline) and queueing-playbook-v1.docx (technical playbook with admission and KV/cache hints).

Karthik — can you confirm the operational feasibility and whether the soft-preemption model works with our current continuous-batching runtime? Also flag any performance regressions we should call out in the redline.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Nina Park <nina.park@starlit.ai>, procurement@starlit.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-28T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool — request for SLA amendment around queueing/tail latency

Hi Nina — following up with a concrete proposal and next steps. Attached are: SLA-amendment-diff.pdf (redline against your current contract) and queueing-playbook-v1.docx (technical playbook). Summary of changes:

- 6-GPU burst reservation (10% of committed capacity) with priority admission for model variant starlit-prod-v2.
- Latency SLOs: 95th <= 120ms, 99th <= 400ms for requests <= 512 tokens.
- Two scheduled maintenance carveouts/month and telemetry retention for 90 days.
- Commercial: monthly reservation fee + per-priority-token surcharge. Exact numbers to follow in the redline (see attachment).

Next steps:
1) Please review the redline. If acceptable, we’ll send for signature via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/STL-2026-1458-sign
2) Technical kickoff: 60-minute session with Karthik and our SRE team to walk the queueing playbook and KV-cache tuning (proposed window: Jan 5–7, 2027). Please share preferred time slots.
3) HubSpot: we’ve captured this in our deal record — https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/2345678

If you want us to broaden the carveouts or change the headroom sizing, tell us which bucket you prefer (more headroom vs higher monthly fee) and we’ll produce an updated proposal.

Thanks again — looking forward to moving this through.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
(attachments: SLA-amendment-diff.pdf, queueing-playbook-v1.docx)
